steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Ottoline Brassbuckle; I hold the keys. This Boiler has been cold since the last tenant left, so stand back. If it holds, it runs your workshop for twelve hours, whether you are here or not.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: It held, which I will admit is a relief. Fifty Brass Ingots from the old stock: set the bench to make spanners, and it works on while you do something else.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: While the spanners turn: this is Story. Each scene is a choice and costs Nerve, which refills with time. The first one is about you, and why No. 9 is yours.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Each spanner takes a little while, and goes into your Stores. Watching does not make it faster, but nobody has ever managed not to watch the first.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: What is that scratching under the floor? Play the next scene; the spanners will keep.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Take up a spanner and go after those rats; the fighting runs by itself, as the bench does. I have left a crate of Rations from the old stock: you eat one whenever a rat hurts you.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Down that hole are the scrapyards, Rustmoor, where the rats live. Beaten, they drop scrap, a Crown or two, and the Umbrella Silk they line their nests with. Keep all of it; ten scraps of silk make hand-wraps.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: The keys are yours now. The bench works on while you are away, and the Boiler fills again each time you come back. That brass tube over the bench has started to rattle: something is on its way.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: The brass tube brought something while you were away. Letters keep until you answer them, but this one will not improve with age.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Pip's bill wants more than a night of rats. The Counting-House window, under Exchange, buys your Rat Scrap on my word, but only so much a week; the rats' Crowns make up the rest.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: The rats have been at your sleeves. Ten scraps of their Umbrella Silk make hand-wraps; wear them and bites hurt less. See the Loadout's Armour line before and after. The note by Start says what happens to the queue.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Nobody has opened Hester's workbench drawer since she left. Clear it out before the day is done; my knees are older than the Boiler.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: That is all the Rat Scrap the window will take this week. Let the rats' Crowns make up the rest, and come back to the window next week.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Do not fret over Rations. You eat one by yourself when a rat hurts you. If you run out, no lasting harm: each time the rats lay you flat you lose a minute, then get up and fight on.
